{{Short description|German-Swiss chemist, university lecturer}}
[[File:Martina Hirayama.jpg|thumb|Image of Martina Hirayama]]
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2024}}
'''Martina Hirayama''' (born 1970) is a German-Swiss [[chemist]], [[university lecturer]] and, since 2019, [[State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation|State Secretary for Education, Research and Innovation (SBFI)]] in Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Der Bundesrat ernennt Martina Hirayama zur neuen Staatssekretärin des SBFI |url=https://www.sbfi.admin.ch/sbfi/de/home/aktuell/medienmitteilungen.msg-id-71466.html |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=www.sbfi.admin.ch}}</ref>

== Life and work ==
Martina Hirayama grew up and went to school in Germany.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Krummenacher |first=Jörg |date=24 April 2019 |title=Staatssekretärin Hirayama zu Horizon, Unis, Berufsbildung |language=de-CH |work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |url=https://www.nzz.ch/schweiz/staatssekretaerin-hirayama-zu-horizon-unis-berufsbildung-ld.1476875 |access-date=2023-11-28 |issn=0376-6829}}</ref> She studied [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Fribourg]] (Switzerland) from 1990 to 1991 and at the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]] (ETH Zurich) in [[Zürich|Zurich]] from 1991 to 1994. She completed her diploma thesis on polymers at [[Imperial College London]] in 1994. She then returned to ETH Zurich, where she completed her doctorate in 1997 at the Institute for Polymers on the "Production and characterization of thin and ultra-thin layers on inorganic surfaces by oxidative addition and activation of chemically reactive bonds" and worked as a [[research assistant]]. From 2001, she was head of the "Polymers on Surfaces" group at the Institute of Polymers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Martina Hirayama |url=https://www.academia-net.org/profile/martina-hirayama/79282 |access-date=28 November 2023 |website=AcademiaNet}}</ref> Hirayama also completed a [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate degree]] in business administration – now called MAS in Management, Technology and Economics – at D-MTEC at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich.

Hirayama focused on application-oriented research and is involved in several patents. She founded a start-up for coating technologies<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bühler |first1=Dennis |last2=Moser |first2=Christof |date=25 June 2019 |title="Die ETH-Leitung hat Fehler gemacht" |url=https://www.republik.ch/2019/06/25/die-eth-leitung-hat-fehler-gemacht |journal=Republik |language=de}}</ref> and moved to [[Zurich University of Applied Sciences/ZHAW|Zurich University of Applied Sciences Winterthur]] (ZHAW) as a lecturer, where she became director of the School of Engineering in 2011 and also took over the International Affairs department in 2014.

Martina Hirayama was president of the Institute Council of the Swiss Federal Institute of Metrology;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Der Bundesrat ernennt Martina Hirayama zur neuen Staatssekretärin des SBFI |url=https://www.news.admin.ch/de/nsb?id=71466 |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=www.admin.ch}}</ref> Vice President of the board of directors of the Innosuisse funding agency and sat on the board of trustees of the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wanner |first1=Aline |last2=Daum |first2=Matthias |last3=Jäggi |first3=Sarah |date=7 January 2019 |title=Frauen: Neues Jahr, neuer Job |language=de-DE |work=Die Zeit |url=https://www.zeit.de/2019/02/frauen-vorhaben-2019-michelle-renaud/seite-2 |access-date=2023-11-28 |issn=0044-2070}}</ref>

Martina Hirayama has been state secretary for education, research and innovation (SBFI) since 1 January 2019. In this role, she is the head of 280 employees and is responsible for an annual [[budget]] of CHF 4.5&nbsp;billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Martina Hirayama |url=https://www.academia-net.org/profile/martina-hirayama/79282 |access-date=28 November 2023 |website=AcademiaNet}}</ref>

Martina Hirayama has held dual German-Swiss [[citizenship]] since 2009.

In 2019, Martina Hirayama took part in the [[Bilderberg Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Participants 2019 |url=https://www.bilderbergmeetings.org/meetings/meeting-2019/participants-2019 |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=www.bilderbergmeetings.org}}</ref>

Hirayama is a member of the Executive Advisory Board of the [[World.minds|World.Minds]] Foundation, where she engages with global leaders on innovation, research, and education policy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Team – WORLD.MINDS |url=https://www.worldminds.org/team/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |language=en}}</ref>
